features.title: Incremental request and tool index from session logs
features.summary: Folds every session log into a SQLite ledger of model requests (agent, subagent, compaction, title, memory and other side calls) with route, tokens, cache reads, stop reason, duration and TTFT, plus privacy-reduced tool execution durations, outcomes and returned-text sizes. Reads only the Zstandard frames each log gained since the last pass. Costs join per-route, per-context-band list prices from the AI Accounts models.dev catalog at query time.
failureModes: A log the writer is still appending to keeps its torn final frame for the next pass instead of failing.
A stored fold state that no longer decodes restarts that log from its first byte; rows upsert by event sequence, so nothing doubles.
Without the AI Accounts price cache every cost reads as unknown (–) and the request still counts.
Title generation keeps no usage in the log: its tokens come only from the live llm/stream observer, so titles generated while the plugin was not loaded show –.
Memory-digest calls are not stored as session-log requests; they are counted only while the live observer is loaded.
A fold-version bump re-reads every session log once so tool rows gain returned-text sizes; until that pass finishes, older rows stay unmeasured.

externalDependencies.boundary: Reads the models.dev price cache AI Accounts writes ($DSH_HOME/plugins/ai-accounts/pricing.json) and its accounts.json for account kinds; never refreshes the catalog itself.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: src/cost.test.ts writes a pricing file in the cache format to a temp directory.

features.title: Request log
features.summary: The Usage: Analytics reusable view with a sortable table of model requests (model and provider, when, project, input, cache read, output, cost, duration, TTFT, status with stop reason), status chips with counts, search by model, provider, project or thread title, a purpose filter and a date range. Each row opens the thread that made the request.
reach: fill textbox "Describe what you want to build, / commands, @ files or sessions" "Seed a usage request"
failureModes: DSH exposes no API to scroll a thread to one turn, so a row opens its thread but cannot jump to the step (see plans/dsh-host-gaps.md).
A subagent session absent from the thread list opens its parent thread instead; an archived or deleted thread shows a notice.

features.title: Usage charts
features.summary: Headline tiles with a previous-period comparison (cost, per day, requests, failures, tokens, cache hit, estimated cache savings and cost per turn), usage over time switchable between cost, tokens and requests and grouped by model, exact provider/account route, project or purpose, a sortable usage distribution table with requests, sessions, average tokens per request, token types, cache share, cost share and estimated cost, and a daily heatmap switchable between tokens, estimated cost and requests for up to a year. Tokens by type, cache hit ratio, requests and failures, TTFT and duration percentiles, and top threads by cost remain available. Missing token and price totals are shown as incomplete. Vendor is not guessed from a route slug and machine is omitted because neither is a reliable captured request dimension.
failureModes: Series beyond the five most expensive fold into Other so the legend stays readable.
Cache savings and cost are list-price estimates from the models.dev catalog; an unpriced route contributes no savings and is counted in the unpriced tally.
A request without a turn (titles and some side calls) does not add a turn, so cost per turn is an average over requests that carry one.

features.title: Jev API usage card
features.summary: The Charts tab shows DSH-origin Jev calls from Backlog and Memory grouped by configured secret-reference or environment-variable label, with provider-reported tokens, request counts, a TypeSafe list-price estimate and calendar month-to-date spend, requests and tokens per label. Bars compare each label's input-token volume with the busiest label this month; they do not represent quota remaining. Labels are local, not provider-verified identity, and usage excludes calls outside DSH.
reach: expect text "Usage by API key · calendar month to date"
failureModes: Calls made outside DSH are not observed; provider-reported balance and account-wide history are not available from the documented Jev API.
Configured credential labels are local references, not proof of provider billing identity; provider account-wide balance/history are not documented API capabilities.
The dshx caller package id is cooperative in-process attribution, not authentication against malicious installed plugins.
Calls without input-token usage remain counted but do not contribute to the estimate.
Per-key bars normalize input tokens to the busiest configured credential in the current calendar month, not to a provider quota or spending cap.
The estimate uses TypeSafe's published $0.042 per million input-token price; update the constant if pricing changes.

features.title: Tool and skill analytics
features.summary: Tool charts over the selected range: calls over time stacked by source category, the ten most-used tools by calls, wall time or estimated returned tokens, a per-category share of returned tokens with success rates, tiles for calls, success rate, interruptions, wall time, returned tokens and the busiest category, plus the per-tool table with outcomes, latency and returned tokens, the top normalized command and test-runner wall-clock distributions, Jev request totals per calling plugin, and recent tool/Jev events. Returned tokens are a characters / 4 estimate of tool result text: only the text length is stored, never the text, and rows indexed before this measurement show as unmeasured. Grouping by category covers skills, plugin API, plugin, MCP, DSH and other tools. Command arguments, paths, outputs, prompts and secrets are never stored; compound or ambiguous shell commands are omitted.
failureModes: Tool records with no result remain unknown or interrupted, not assumed successful.
A tool result with no text (an image, or a record written before returned tokens were measured) keeps the call but adds no tokens; the row shows the measured share.
An hourly timeline request over more than two days coarsens to daily buckets so the response stays bounded.
Jev figures cover only calls Backlog and Memory record through recordJevUsage; calls made while Usage analytics is not loaded are not counted.
Returned tokens are estimated from text characters, not provider-reported usage, so they approximate context cost rather than billing.

features.title: OTLP metrics export
features.summary: The read-only usage_otel_metrics Agent tool returns an OTLP/HTTP JSON metrics request from the local SQLite usage ledger. It includes model requests and token use, tool category/source counts and Jev requests per calling plugin with token counters and duration histograms. It never makes a network request; quota and Fast-mode history remain in AI Accounts storage.
failureModes: An export range wider than 365 days is rejected.
Named tool source points cap at 500 while category totals remain exact.
OTLP output is delta temporality; overlapping imports can double count, so consumers must select non-overlapping intervals.
